messages:
emma: FYI — after a hardware-induced NIC flap in us-west-2 we triggered DNS-based failover to us-west-1 at ~12:10UTC. Most traffic moved but support is seeing a fraction of clients still hitting the old egress IP and returning 503s. Lots of variance across ISPs.

raj: digging now. `dig @1.1.1.1 app.redwood.ai A +short` still returns the old IP for me. Looks like the failover record had TTL=3600. Who authored that? :eyes:

emma: that was me — bad oversight during the runbook update. I pushed a change to set TTL=30s in Route53 at 12:12 but seeing slow propagation to some resolvers.

liam: route53 update helps authoritative servers, but many ISP resolvers will honor older TTLs until expiry. We should also purge any CDN edge caches and see if we can request cache flushes from large DNS resolvers where possible.

emma: Purged Fastly and CloudFront at 12:14. Also filed cache purge with DNS provider support for specific resolver ranges (asking them to accelerate).

raj: for visibility, here's a quick check I ran:
```
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 app.redwood.ai | sort | uniq -c
  42 203.0.113.12  <-- old egress (us-west-2)
 158 198.51.100.9  <-- new egress (us-west-1)
```
So ~20% of queries still hit old IP.

liam: question — are any customers hard-pinning IPs (on-prem customers, edge appliances)? If so, they won't respect TTL.

dns-team: quick check in support logs shows 6 enterprise customers with appliances that pin the A record. We sent tickets to account teams to notify them.

emma: two operational paths: (A) attempt a targeted BGP announcement to shift the old IP to the new region (fast but high risk/hard to rollback), or (B) scale us-west-2 capacity back up to absorb leftover traffic while TTLs drain.

sre-oncall: current us-west-2 GPU pool is at ~65% utilization but showing spike in pod evictions. We can spin 4 extra p4d hosts in ~12–18 minutes with emergency quota — cost hit ~+$8k/day but will avoid errors.

liam: if we scale, also reduce per-model concurrency and aggressive batch sizes to reduce memory pressure. Patch the runtime config: set `max_concurrency=2` and `batch_target_tokens=512` for affected pools.

emma: applied autoscale override +4 nodes at 12:20 and pushed temporary runtime caps. Started rolling back canaries to lower memory footprint.

ops-bot: deploy job `emergency-scale` started by emma — 4 nodes provisioning (estimated ready 12:34UTC).

raj: continuing DNS side — we can also create a very short-lived A record alias for the old IP with TTL=10s and flip it to a sinkhole that returns TCP reset, to force clients to re-resolve. Risky for stateful connections though. Thoughts?

liam: I'd avoid sinkhole unless we know sessions are ephemeral. Prefer scaling and letting TTLs drain — safer.

emma: agreed. we'll hold scaling and TTL strategy. Monitoring: real user errors drop from ~8% -> ~1.2% after new hosts come up. Still seeing intermittent 503s from specific ISPs.

dns-team: we received confirmation from our DNS provider that a small set of resolvers (major ISP X) cache A records aggressively; they manually flushed their edge cache for our zone. That reduced residual traffic to old IP by ~75% for affected prefix.

raj: note for post-incident — failover record TTL should be 60s (min) and we need a preflight run that lowers TTLs to 30–60s 30 minutes before any planned failover. Add check to runbook to ensure no one commits long TTL on ephemeral failover entries.

emma: added runbook change and created a short checklist:
- set failover TTL=60s
- pre-warm target region (GPU pool >=30% headroom)
- purge CDN edges + request resolver flush for major ISPs if possible
- avoid sinkhole unless emergency

liam: also add a step to notify account teams about pinned-IP customers and provide mitigation (proxy config or manual reconfigure).

sre-oncall: cost note: emergency +4 p4d nodes ~+$8k/day, we kept them for 2.5 hours then scaled down. Estimated incremental cost this incident: ~$800.

emma: closing notes: residual impact resolved ~12:50UTC after provisioning + resolver flushes. Postmortem in progress, will include a timeline and updated TTL defaults. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
